Description [en]: The product's name. DO NOT TRANSLATE. Keep exactly as written, with a capital M, W and S.
Short form of the product's name. DO NOT TRANSLATE.
Abbreviation of ModWarden Suite. DO NOT TRANSLATE.
The paid plan's name. DO NOT TRANSLATE. Always written Pro, with a capital P.
The free plan's name, used as a name (the Free plan). Keep it as a name; translate the word free only when it is not the plan's name.
The chat app the bot runs in. DO NOT TRANSLATE.
Streaming site. DO NOT TRANSLATE.
Streaming site (kick.com), written with a capital K. DO NOT TRANSLATE when it means the site. Not the same as kick, removing a member.
Video site. DO NOT TRANSLATE.
YouTube's live streams. DO NOT TRANSLATE.
Video app. DO NOT TRANSLATE.
TikTok's live streams, written in capitals. DO NOT TRANSLATE.
Website of communities (subreddits). DO NOT TRANSLATE.
A kind of web feed. DO NOT TRANSLATE.
The website's address. DO NOT TRANSLATE.
Experience points members earn by chatting. Keep XP unless your language has a well-known gaming term for it, and then use that everywhere.
A Discord server (a community). Use the word Discord itself uses in your language, never a word meaning a computer server.
A Discord text or voice channel. Use Discord's own word in your language.
A Discord role, which gives members a colour and permissions. Use Discord's own word in your language.
Someone in a Discord server. Use Discord's own word in your language.
To notify someone by mentioning them or their role, as in Ping this role. Use Discord's word for mention or notify in your language.
Naming a member or role in a message with @, which notifies them. Use Discord's own word in your language.
Discord's way of stopping a member from talking for a while. Use Discord's own word in your language.
Removing a member from the server; they can rejoin with an invite. Use Discord's own word in your language. Not the streaming site Kick.
Removing a member from the server so they cannot rejoin. Use Discord's own word in your language.
A note on a member's record that they broke a rule. Several can lead to a timeout or ban.
Discord's permission that allows everything in a server. Use Discord's own word in your language.
A command members type starting with /, such as /rank. Use Discord's own term in your language. The command names themselves are never translated.
A Discord thread: a side conversation under a message. Use Discord's own word in your language.
A boxed message the bot posts, with a coloured stripe. If your language has no word for it, describe it as a message box.
The people who run and moderate a server: moderators and admins.
The name staff replies appear under, so members never see which person answered. Translate as the team, never as one person.
A level of staff, such as Moderator or Admin, each with its own permissions in the bot.
A staff member who keeps the server safe.
Private conversations between a member and the staff team, held through the bot. Many languages keep the English word.
A member asking for a ban or warning to be looked at again.
A form a member fills in to ask for something, such as becoming a moderator.
One moderation action (warning, timeout, kick or ban) with its number, reason and evidence.
Screenshots, messages and notes kept with a case to show why it was taken.
The record of everything that happened in a server and everything staff did.
The ModWarden Suite website where staff set the bot up, at mwsbot.app.
The bot's settings for a whole server, changed by its staff. Always this word for Settings, and never the same word as Preferences.
One staff member's own choices for how the panel looks (colours, text size). Never the same word as Settings.
A stage members reach by earning XP.
A member's position on the server's leaderboard, such as #4.
The image showing a member's level, rank and XP.
The list of members with the most XP.
How many days in a row a member has chatted.
The panel page for welcome and leave messages and welcome cards.
The image posted when someone joins, with their picture and name.
A prize draw members enter with a button.
A trap channel: anyone who posts in it is banned, which catches spam bots and hacked accounts.
Many accounts joining at once to spam or disrupt a server.
Stopping everyone except staff from posting, for a while.
New members confirming they are a real person before they can talk.
The feature that removes spam such as mass mentions and repeated messages.
A reply the bot sends when a message matches a trigger.
Members giving themselves roles by pressing a button or reaction.
A post in Discord when a streamer goes live.
A source of posts (a subreddit or an RSS feed) that the bot announces.
